stem: A chemist mixes \(x\) liters of a 20% acid solution with \(y\) liters of a 50% acid solution. The equation \(0.2x + 0.5y = 15\) represents the combinations that contain exactly 15 liters of pure acid. The graph of this equation in the \(xy\)-plane has a \(y\)-intercept of \((0, 30)\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of this \(y\)-intercept?

choices.A: 30 liters of the 20% solution, with none of the 50% solution, contain 15 liters of pure acid.
choices.B: 30 liters of the 50% solution, with none of the 20% solution, contain 15 liters of pure acid.
choices.C: Every mixture on the graph has a total volume of 30 liters.
choices.D: Each liter of the 50% solution contains 30 milliliters of pure acid.

solution: At the \(y\)-intercept, \(x = 0\): no 20% solution is used.
Then \(0.5y = 15\), so \(y = 30\): 30 liters of the 50% solution alone contain 15 liters of acid.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The \(y\)-intercept has \(x = 0\), so it uses none of the 20% solution. (30 liters of the 20% solution contain only 6 liters of acid.)
explanation.B: Correct. At \(x = 0\), \(0.5y = 15\) gives \(y = 30\): 30 liters of the 50% solution alone contain 15 liters of acid.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The intercept is one point on the graph; other combinations, such as \(x = 75, y = 0\), have different total volumes.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Each liter of the 50% solution contains 0.5 liter of acid; 30 is a number of liters of solution, not an amount per liter.

verify:
y = symbols('y')
assert solve(Eq(Rational(5, 10)*y, 15), y) == [30]
assert choices[answer].startswith('30 liters of the 50% solution')
